A large black circular arrow goes around the Earth and the Sun, starting near the Sun's lower left, passing under the Earth and ending with an arrowhead at the right of the Sun.
figures.original: Which picture is right, A or B?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 2 Learners Book PDF
figures.shows: Three cartoon children stand side by side: one in a green top and blue trousers, one in an orange top and olive trousers with hands on hips, and one in a yellow top with a red star and dark trousers. Each child has a very long dark shadow that stretches down toward the bottom of the picture. The letter B is in the top left corner.
figures.original: Look at these pictures. a Is the Sun high or low in these pictures? b Do you think it is morning, midday or evening?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Two panels show an investigation with three small green seedlings in black pots next to a window with a bright sun. In the left panel, labelled "light", an open cardboard box stands beside the pots and the plants are in the light. In the right panel, labelled "no light", the box is turned over and moved down over the pots, shown by a red arrow, so the plants are covered and get no light.
figures.original: Look at the pictures to see what to do.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Three panels each show three small green seedlings in black pots and a green watering can, with a row of day letters m t w t f s s. In the first panel all seven days are ticked, and the caption is 'Water every day.' In the second panel only two days (Monday and Thursday) are ticked, and the caption is 'Water twice a week.' In the third panel the watering can is crossed out in red and no days are ticked, and the caption is 'Do not water.'
figures.original: Look at the pictures to see what to do. What do you predict will happen to the plants' leaves, stems and roots in each case?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A drawing of a model flower made from craft materials. It has a yellow flower head with five pointed petals and an orange circular centre, on a white stem. Two green leaves are tied to the stem with thread, and loose grey threads hang from the bottom of the stem as roots. No labels are printed.
figures.original: Make a plant like this one.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A drawing of a flowering plant with purple petals around a yellow centre, a green stem with four green leaves, and branching roots. Four labelled lines point to parts: D points to a petal of the flower, C points to a leaf on the right side, B points to the stem, and A points to a root.
figures.original: Here is a flowering plant. Copy and complete these sentences. A is the ______. B is the ______. C is a ______. D is the ______.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A four-panel chart with a blue border. Each panel has a word label and a picture: 'water' with a jug of water, 'light' with a yellow sun, 'food' with a loaf of bread and slices, and 'plant pot' with a dark plant pot.
figures.original: Which two of these does a plant need for it to to grow?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Three numbered cartoon panels show an experiment. In panel 1 a girl places half an egg shell into each of two cups. In panel 2 she pours water into one cup and a sugary drink from a bottle into the other. In panel 3, after seven days, she holds the cup with the sugary drink and looks at a crumbling egg shell, while the other cup stays on the table.
labels: Place half an egg shell into each cup.
Add water to one cup and a sugary drink to the other.
After seven days see what has happened to the egg shell.
figures.original: Look at the pictures to see what to do. Predict what you think will happen to the egg shells.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A table with the column headings 'Fruit/Vegetable', 'Prediction' and 'Result'. Under Prediction is 'Will you like it?'. Under Result are 'How did it taste?' and 'Did you like it?'. One row is filled in: melon, no, very sweet, yes. One blank row is below it.
figures.original: Draw a table like this for your results.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A colored drawing of a meal on a green mat. A plate holds spaghetti topped with red tomato sauce and green basil leaves, with a fork on the left of the plate and a knife on the right. An orange sits at the upper left and a glass of water sits at the upper right. Nothing is labelled.
figures.original: Here is a healthy meal. Explain why it is healthy.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Two cartoon-style drawings of sandwiches labelled A and B. Sandwich A has yellow bread with lettuce leaves and tomato slices between the slices. Sandwich B has white bread with a dark red jam-like spread oozing out of the filling.
figures.original: Which sandwich is more healthy? Why?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Four drinks are drawn, each with a label giving its sugar content per 100ml. A water bottle says sugar 0g, a red cola can says sugar 11g, an orange carton with a blue straw says sugar 10g, and a purple blackcurrant carton says sugar 5g.
figures.original: These drinks have different amounts of sugar per 100ml.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Eight circular photographs with coloured borders, in two rows of four. The top row shows a burning match, a macaw flying, a stone moai statue on a grassy hill, and a tree covered in white blossom. The bottom row shows a space shuttle launching with a trail of flame, a pink jellyfish in water, a peacock butterfly on yellow flowers, and a desktop computer monitor with a keyboard and mouse.
figures.original: Which things in these pictures are alive?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A cartoon zookeeper in a green shirt with a 'Z' badge stands thinking, with thought bubbles around her showing eight animal heads: a lion, a swan, a mouse, a pelican, a lizard or snake-like reptile, a panda, an eagle and a crocodile. Below her are three cages with signs reading 'Animals with feathers', 'Animals with fur' and 'Animals with scales'.
figures.original: Help the zookeeper sort the animals into the correct group.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Two rows of six colored square cards, each with a drawing of a living thing. The top row shows a blue butterfly, a brown bear, a blue lupin plant with a flower spike, a black ant, a red flower with green leaves, and a yellow-gold fish. The bottom row shows a brown monkey, a small green-yellow fish, a brown scorpion, a silver spotted fish, a white goat, and a green plant with yellow flowers.
figures.original: Look at these pictures. Talk to a friend about how you could sort these living things.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A photograph of two large grey-blue herons at a nest made of sticks and twigs among green leaves. One heron stands upright behind with a long yellow beak, and the other leans forward over the nest with its neck stretched down, touching the sticks with its beak. The photo is set in a circular frame with a purple border.
figures.original: Name an animal and the shelter it makes for its eggs or young.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Three circular close-ups of fingerprints, each with a coloured border and a label beneath it. The left one, with a blue border, is labelled 'loop'. The middle one, with a pink border, is labelled 'arch'. The right one, with a green border, is labelled 'whorl'.
figures.original: Look at your fingers. Use a magnifying glass if possible. Identify which type of fingerprint you have.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A two-column table with the headings "Animal" and "Number of young produced". The rows are: rabbit, 8; birds, 6; human, 1 or 2; fish, 1000s of eggs; spiders, 100s of eggs.
figures.original: Which animals can have the most young?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A drawing of a rose plant growing in a brown flowerpot. It has one green stem with several green leaves and a single red flower at the top. The pot is filled with brown soil. There are no labels.
figures.original: For this plant, which questions are 'true' and which questions are 'false'?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Eight colored square cards, each with one cartoon-style drawing. The top row shows a boy in a red and white striped shirt, a brown bear, a mouse, and a blue and purple butterfly. The bottom row shows a monkey, a white goat, a lion, and a grey elephant.
figures.original: Which of these animals do you think can smell things the best?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Eight separate colour drawings with no labels: a cuckoo clock, an eagle in flight, a lit tealight candle, a yellow Volkswagen Beetle car, a green frog with dark spots, and a yellow-flowered dandelion plant. Below these are a white cloud and a yellow sun partly covered by streaks of cloud.
figures.original: Magda's book contains pictures of these things. Help her to say which are alive and which are not alive.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A table with two columns headed 'Material' and 'Properties'. The first row has 'paper' under Material and 'weak, flexible, smooth, absorbent' under Properties. The second row is empty.
figures.original: Draw a table like this and write down the properties of the materials.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A bar chart titled by its axes: the vertical axis is 'Number of children' with gridlines at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50, and the horizontal axis is 'Eye colour'. There are three bars: grey is about 13, brown is about 41, and blue is about 38.
figures.original: Alex has recorded the eye colour of the children in his school on this graph. a Which is the most common eye colour? b Which is the least common eye colour?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A table with columns Name, Food, Like and Dislike, listing four children, each with apple and biscuit rows. Bill, Jaffa and Rava have a tick under Like for both apple and biscuit. Pat has a tick under Dislike for apple and a tick under Like for biscuit.
figures.original: a Which food is most popular?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A photograph of a life-size car sculpted entirely from clear, pale blue ice. It sits on a dark display platform at what looks like a car show, with a blue backdrop and a Ford logo at the right edge. The car is a convertible with an open top, and its wheels are also made of ice.
figures.original: Why is a car made of ice a silly idea?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A branching sorting chart (decision tree) starting with the question "Is it hard?" with yes and no arrows. The yes arrow leads to "Is it shiny?" and the no arrow leads to "Is it waterproof?". Each of these has yes and no arrows that end in empty question marks. A yellow side panel lists four objects with pictures: brick, balloon, paper (shown as a tissue box) and ice (a melting ice cube).
figures.original: Choose one of the four objects and answer the questions.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A Venn diagram made of two overlapping circles. The left circle is labelled "flexible" and the right circle is labelled "hard". The overlap is empty, and so are the rest of both circles.
figures.original: Copy this Venn diagram and write the following objects in the right places.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A hand holds a red horseshoe magnet with grey tips, and the tips point to the right. Wavy lines next to each tip show the magnetic pull. A red toy car with blue-grey windows and wheels sits to the right of the magnet, facing right, with its back end toward the magnet.
figures.original: Draw a picture to show what will happen to the metal toy car.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A table with three columns headed Object, Magnetic and Non-magnetic. The Object column has four rows, each with a label and a drawing: a metal can, a book, a football and metal scissors. The Magnetic and Non-magnetic cells are all empty.
figures.original: Copy and complete this table.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A table with four column headings: Object, Material, Magnetic and Non-magnetic. The one filled row reads chair, plastic, with a red tick in the Non-magnetic column and the Magnetic column left empty.
figures.original: Draw a table like this one for your results.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A bar chart with the vertical axis 'Force in newtons (N)' numbered 0 to 5 and the horizontal axis 'Type of surface'. There are three bars. Wood is a brown bar at about 1.5 N, grass is a green bar at about 3.5 N, and stone is a grey bar at about 1 N.
figures.original: Which surface was the hardest to pull the skateboard on?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: Three forcemeters (newton meters) labelled A, B and C, each with a ring at the top, a red adjuster, a vertical slot with a scale of tick marks, and a hook at the bottom. Each has a yellow marker band with a value: A shows 5N, B shows 10N and C shows 20N. The yellow band sits higher on A, lower on B and lowest on C, near the bottom of the slot.
figures.original: Which forcemeter is measuring the greatest force?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A partly drawn bar chart with the vertical axis 'Plant height in cm' numbered 0 to 10. The first bar, 'Plant with water', has its top drawn at 8 cm, with its left and right sides drawn in black. A pencil points at the bottom of the right side at 2 cm. The second category, 'Plant with no water', has no bar drawn.
figures.original: Draw the sides of the first bar. Use a ruler.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A bar chart on lined paper with the vertical axis 'Plant height in cm' numbered 0 to 10. The bar for 'Plant with water' is drawn up to 8 cm. The bar for 'Plant with no water' is drawn up to 4 cm, with a pencil at its bottom right corner.
figures.original: Draw the second bar the same way. Use a ruler.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 3 Learners
figures.shows: A table with two columns and one row of data. The left column is headed "Plant height with water in cm" and holds the value 8. The right column is headed "Plant height with no water in cm" and holds the value 4.
labels: Plant height with water in cm
Plant height with no water in cm
figures.original: Look at the table. The numbers tell you how tall to make each bar.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A table with three columns headed Josie, Yasmin and Luisa, and one row labelled 'Bone length in cm'. The values are 25 for Josie, 32 for Yasmin and 28 for Luisa.
figures.original: Josie, Yasmin and Luisa measured the length of their upper arm bones. These are their results.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A drawing of a bent human arm showing the bones of the shoulder, upper arm and forearm with two muscles on the upper arm. Label 1 points to the muscle on the front of the upper arm, and label 2 points to the muscle on the back of the upper arm. The forearm is bent at the elbow.
figures.original: Look at the drawing and answer the questions.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: Six cartoon-style drawings of animals, each on a coloured square in two rows of three. Top row: a brown mouse on green, a brown rabbit on purple, a patterned grey and brown snake coiled on pale blue. Bottom row: a goldfish in a round fish bowl on red, a white and brown cat sitting on blue, a small brown rodent with a long tufted tail on red.
figures.original: Construct a key to identify these pets.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A bar chart with the vertical axis labelled 'Manure in tonnes', running from 0 to 20 in steps of 5. The horizontal axis lists the days Sunday to Saturday. Bar heights are: Sunday about 18, Monday 15, Tuesday 20, Wednesday 10, Thursday no bar (0), Friday 20, Saturday 15.
figures.original: Each day, Tabansi the farmer dumps manure from his animals on the land next to the river. The bar chart shows how many tonnes he dumps each day in one week.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: Four drawings, each inside a screen-like frame, arranged in a 2 by 2 grid. Top left: two fish swim in water among green water plants, with rocks on the bottom. Top right: a camel stands on yellow sand dunes under a bright sun, with a small spiky plant beside it. Bottom left: a green spotted frog sits on grass beside a pond with reeds and white flowers. Bottom right: a bald eagle with wings spread flies in front of a snow-capped mountain.
figures.original: Write the name of the habitat shown in each picture.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A particle model with 13 identical blue spheres on a white background. The spheres are spread far apart in an irregular, random arrangement, and none of them touch. There are no labels or printed values.
figures.original: Does the diagram below represent a model of a solid, a liquid or a gas?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: An old-fashioned gramophone (phonograph) in an oval frame. It has a square, dark patterned wooden box with a round turntable on top, a small label on the front and a hand crank on the right side. A curved arm holds a needle over the turntable and leads up to a large brass horn that flares outwards.
figures.original: Look at the picture. How do you think the music was made louder?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A table with two columns headed 'Material' and 'Loudness of sound'. The Material column lists air, water and wood in three rows. The 'Loudness of sound' cells are all empty, to be filled in by the learner.
figures.original: Which material did you hear the sound best through?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: Three musical instruments are drawn and labelled A, B and C. A is a pair of yellow cymbals, each with a brown leather strap. B is a grey-blue woodwind instrument with a white mouthpiece, a row of finger holes and cream-coloured rings. C is a yellow harp with a tall pillar, a curved top and many vertical strings.
figures.original: Look at the pictures of these musical instruments.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a tambourine, a round musical instrument with a wooden frame, a skin head and metal jingles set into the rim. A person's hand with a ring on one finger rests on the skin head. The caption below reads 'tambourine'.
figures.original: Look at each of these instruments. Which of these have you seen and heard?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: Eight identical glass bottles stand in a row on a line, numbered 1 to 8 below. Bottle 1 has a little water, and the water level rises in each bottle up to bottle 8, which is almost full. A bracket at the left marks the 'Column of air' above the water in bottle 1. Callouts say to pour a little water into bottle 1, a little more into bottle 2, and that bottle 8 must be almost full.
labels: Pour a little water into this bottle.
Pour a little more water into this bottle.
This bottle must be almost full.
figures.original: Predict what pitch of sounds you will make when you blow across the other bottles.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A battery lies on its side with its negative (−) end on the left and its positive (+) end on the right. A piece of tape holds one end of an orange wire to the + end. The wire runs in a loop to one terminal of a bulb holder, with arrows along the wire pointing from the + end towards the bulb. A second wire goes from the other terminal of the bulb holder back to the − end of the battery. The yellow bulb sits on a teal stepped base. The wire is attached to the − end only by its position, with no tape shown there. The arrows show the direction along the whole loop, from the battery's + end, through the bulb, and back to the − end.
figures.original: Look at the diagram. Predict what will happen to the bulb in this circuit.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A cutaway diagram of the inside of a torch. Two cells are stacked one above the other, each with a yellow + end at the top and a grey - end at the bottom. A bulb sits at the top inside a reflector, with labels pointing to the 'bulb' and the 'cell'. A yellow metal strip, a switch and a spring at the bottom complete the circuit. Arrows show the current going up the side strip, across the top to the bulb, and then down through the cells.
labels: The inside of a torch. The arrows show which way the electric current goes.
figures.original: What happens if you put the two positive terminals of the cells in a torch together? Will the bulb light up?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A series circuit drawn as apparatus: a battery pack of cells held together with tape, with a plus sign on one end, is joined by orange wires to a switch made from a wooden block with a paper clip and two drawing pins. The circuit continues through three bulbs, each on a green stepped holder, in a single loop back to the battery. The switch is drawn with the paper clip touching one pin at its end, and no bulbs are shown lit. The figure is marked with the number 1.
figures.original: Close the switch. Observe the bulbs. Open the switch.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A drawing of a series circuit with a battery (cell) taped in a holder with the + end at the left, and two bulbs on green round bulb holders. Orange wires join the battery to the first bulb holder, the first bulb holder to the second bulb holder, and the second bulb holder to a wooden block switch. The switch is made from a paper clip and two metal fasteners (drawing pins). A wire from the switch returns to the battery's + end at the left.
figures.original: Describe the path of the electricity in the circuit you made.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A yellow ruler marked 0 to 15 is drawn along the bottom, with a bar magnet above it. The magnet's left half is red and labelled N, and its right half is blue and labelled S. A paperclip touches the N end of the magnet, with its left end near the 6 mark and the magnet spanning roughly 7 to 12 on the ruler. A black arrow at the top points toward the magnet.
figures.original: Stop the magnet as soon as the paperclip is attracted to and touches the magnet. Read off the distance in mm on the ruler. This is the first reading.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A drawing of a series electric circuit. A battery with its minus end on the left and its plus end on the right is connected by orange wires to two lamps on teal bases, and to a switch on a wooden block. The switch is labelled A and has two metal contacts joined by a metal clip. All the parts are joined in one loop.
figures.original: In the circuit below:

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 4 Learners
figures.shows: A drawing of a simple electric circuit. A cell with its + end at the top left and its − end on the right is held with tape. Orange wires connect the cell to a switch made of a paper clip and two metal fasteners on a wooden block, and to a buzzer. The buzzer has its − and + terminals marked. The drawing gives no voltage values.
figures.original: A 1.5 V cell is used with a 3 V buzzer. Will the buzzer work? Explain your answer.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: Two drawings of a bean-shaped yellow seed. The left one is the whole seed with a 'food store' label pointing to the yellow body and a 'scar where seed was joined to fruit' label pointing to a small mark on its edge. The right one is a cross-section with a thin brown 'seed coat' around the outside and a small green 'embryo' at the top, next to the yellow interior.
labels: scar where seed was joined to fruit
figures.topic: The life cycle of flowering plants
figures.original: Draw and label the inside parts of the seed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A table with three columns headed 'Name', 'How the plants looked' and 'Growth of plants in cm'. Ashok: green and healthy, 25. Marco: lighter green and quite healthy, 18. Leo: dry and brown, 6. Tariq: thin and weak, 14.
figures.original: Draw a bar chart of the results.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: Two potted plants are drawn side by side. The left plant has a single bent stem that droops over, with a few yellow, wilted leaves and no flowers. The right plant has several large, bright green rounded leaves and two clusters of red flowers on upright stems.
figures.original: Look at these pictures. Which plant is healthy and growing well?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: Two drawings of the same red-flowered geranium plant in a brown pot, labelled Plant A and Plant B. Plant A sits on a windowsill in front of a glass window, with a sun in the upper right pane. Plant B sits inside a dark, closed-in space with a yellow door open beside it, so it is in a dark cupboard-like place.
figures.original: Look at the pictures to see what to do.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: Two separate tables side by side. Column A lists five numbered words: 1 seed, 2 embryo, 3 seed coat, 4 germinate, 5 environment. Column B lists five lettered meanings: A the outer cover that protects the seed, B when a seed start to grow, C everything around us, D part of a plant that can grow into a new plant, E part of a seed that grows into a new plant.
labels: the outer cover that protects the seed
when a seed start to grow
part of a plant that can grow into a new plant
part of a seed that grows into a new plant
figures.topic: The life cycle of flowering plants
figures.original: Match the words in column A with their meanings in column B.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A drawing of a germinating seed, yellow and rounded like a maize grain, with four parts marked by numbered label lines. Label 1 points to the thin green shoot growing up from the top of the seed. Label 2 points to the large yellow body of the seed. Label 3 points to a small orange-brown part at the bottom of the seed. Label 4 points to a pale root growing downward from the base of the seed.
figures.topic: The life cycle of flowering plants
figures.original: Here is a picture of a germinating seed. Write down the names of parts 1 to 4.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A table with two columns headed "Conditions" and "Number of seeds germinated". The rows are: warm, light = 10; warm, dark = 15; cold, light = 5; cold, dark = 7.
figures.original: Dembe's class germinated seeds under different conditions. These are their results.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a branch of a bush willow with green leaves. Several reddish-brown seeds hang from thin stalks along the branch, and each seed has a papery, wing-like outer part surrounding a small green central body. The caption reads 'Bush willow seed.'
figures.topic: The life cycle of flowering plants
figures.original: How do think the bush willow seed is dispersed? Give a reason for your answer.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of two grass-like flower spikes, probably wheat or barley, on a dark background. Each spike has long thin bristles (awns) at the tip. Many small yellow stamens hang down from along the sides of each spike. The photograph is labelled A.
figures.topic: The life cycle of flowering plants
figures.original: Look at the pictures of the two flowers.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a single carnation flower with many frilly-edged petals. The petals are white with pink-red streaks and stripes. A short green stem is visible at the lower right, and the background is blurred green and yellow. The letter B is printed below the photograph.
figures.topic: The life cycle of flowering plants
figures.original: Look at the pictures of the two flowers.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: Two drawings labelled A and B. A shows a winged seed (like a sycamore or maple fruit) with two flat, pale, wing-like parts joined at a green centre with a small stalk on top. B shows an open green pod with round seeds inside and several seeds falling out, with curly tendrils at the bottom.
figures.topic: The life cycle of flowering plants
figures.original: How are the seeds shown in the pictures spread? Give a reason for your answers.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A diagram split by a thick orange vertical wall. On the left, a sun with short wavy lines around it sits above a glass of water, and the glass casts a grey shadow on the ground. On the right, a grey shaded area, where the sun does not reach, holds an identical glass of water. Each glass has a line marking the starting water level, and the water in both glasses looks about the same height. There are no printed labels or values.
figures.original: Which glass had the least water and which glass had the most water after two days? Suggest reasons for this.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A drawing of a flat wooden rack with a mesh base divided into six sections. Bunches of green grapes lie on the mesh, and a few loose grapes are in one section. A bright yellow sun with rays is drawn above the rack. The caption reads 'grapes drying on a rack in the sun'.
figures.original: Talk about how evaporation happens in each of the pictures and how it is useful.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A drawing of a front-loading tumble dryer with its door open. Inside the drum are brightly coloured clothes in pink, green and yellow. The caption underneath reads 'using a tumble dryer'.
figures.original: Talk about how evaporation happens in each of the pictures and how it is useful.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book
figures.shows: A diagram of the water cycle. A sun is at top left, and wavy arrows rise from the sea toward a white cloud, with label line A pointing to the arrows. A block arrow points from the white cloud to a grey rain cloud, with label line B pointing to the arrow. Rain falls from the grey cloud onto green mountains with a snow-capped peak, and a small white cloud beside the peak drops snow or hail, with label line C pointing to that cloud. A river runs down the land into the sea, and label line D points to the green land.
figures.original: Label the processes that take place at points A-D on the diagram of the water cycle.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Science 5 Learners Book

figures.original: Arrange the two mirrors upright and at right angles to each other. Place your small object where the two mirrors meet.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A table with three rows and three columns. Each cell holds a phrase describing something that could be measured. the distance of a marathon race
the length of a long journey

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3

It spans 2 squares across and 2 squares up, starting at the second vertical line and the fourth horizontal line. There are no labels or numbers.
figures.original: Draw three lines to make this into a square. Estimate and then measure the length of one side.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A table with four columns headed Length, Width, Perimeter (cm) and Area (square units). There are four empty rows, and the Area column holds the value 20 in every row. The Length, Width and Perimeter cells are blank.
figures.original: On centimetre squared paper, draw four different rectangles with an area of 20 square cm. Complete this table.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3

figures.original: These squares are drawn on centimetre squared paper. Explain what happens to the perimeter when the squares get bigger.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Twelve separate outlined 2D shapes with no labels or colour. They are: an equilateral triangle, a tall thin rectangle, a semicircle, a regular pentagon, a thin slanted quadrilateral (trapezium-like), a scalene triangle, a regular octagon, a tall thin isosceles triangle, an irregular concave hexagon-like shape, another regular octagon, an irregular pentagon, a trapezium-like quadrilateral with slanted top, and an elongated irregular hexagon.
figures.original: a Colour the regular shapes. b Draw a ring around the irregular shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Six colored flat shapes in a row, with no labels. From left to right: a green arrowhead (concave) shape with a notch at the top; a purple trapezium that is narrower at the top than the bottom; a tall thin dark blue rectangle; a red square turned to stand on a corner (a diamond); a blue parallelogram-like slanted shape with a slanted left side and a long diagonal edge; and a light blue square.
figures.original: Complete the sentences to describe these shapes in three different ways.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A French road sign with a yellow label 'D 156' above a white arrow-shaped board pointing right. The board reads 'PEYREMALE 10' and 'BESSÈGES 16'. Beside it is a smaller marker post sign with 'D 156' and an arrow, and the number 0 underneath.
figures.original: a Round up to the nearest 10 km. b Round down to the nearest 5 km.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A square grid of light blue lines, 6 squares wide and 6 squares tall. A red square labelled "A" is drawn on the grid lines and covers 3 by 3 grid squares. It sits one square in from the left and top edges and two squares in from the right and bottom edges.
figures.original: Is its perimeter 9 cm? Explain your answer.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A yellow-orange rectangle labelled with the letter C at its top left. The top side is labelled 7 m and the right side is labelled 2 m.
figures.original: Work out the perimeters of these shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A blue-filled quadrilateral with four straight sides. The top side is labelled 7 cm, the left side 2 cm, the bottom-left side 6 cm, and the right side 5 cm. The top side is the longest horizontal edge, and the bottom edge slopes down to the right.
figures.original: Work out the perimeters of these shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A pink triangle with side lengths printed along its edges: 7 km on the left side, 10 km on the upper right side, and 11 km on the bottom side. The letters e and f are printed in red outside the triangle, e at the upper left and f at the right.
figures.original: Work out the perimeters of these shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A green pentagon shaped like an arrow or house on its side. It has a rectangular left part with a flat left side and a pointed right end. figures.original: Work out the perimeters of these shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A single purple zigzag line on a light blue background, made of straight segments. It rises from the lower left to a first peak, dips to a low point, rises to a higher peak near the upper right, then falls steeply to the lower right. There are no labels, numbers or scale printed on it.
figures.original: 2 Measure the lengths of each of these lines.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3

figures.original: Estimate, measure and calculate the area of these shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A square grid of small squares, 6 squares wide and 6 squares tall, drawn with light blue lines. An orange square covers the inner 4 by 4 squares, leaving a one-square border of uncoloured squares all the way around it.
figures.original: Estimate, measure and calculate the area of these shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A rectangular grid of small squares, 5 squares wide and 3 squares tall. A green shaded rectangle covers the middle row, spanning the 3 middle columns (from the second to the fourth column), so it is 3 squares long and 1 square high. A partial letter 'c' is visible at the left edge outside the grid.
figures.original: Estimate, measure and calculate the area of these shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A grid of small squares, 3 columns wide and 8 rows tall. A yellow-orange rectangle fills the middle column from the second row to the seventh row, so it is 1 square wide and 6 squares tall. The rows at the top and bottom and the columns on either side are empty. A letter 'd' is partly visible at the top left corner.
figures.original: Estimate, measure and calculate the area of these shapes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Two shapes are drawn on a square grid. On the left is a pink shape that looks like a block with a notch cut out of the bottom. It is 4 squares wide across the top, with a rectangular gap in the bottom edge and a foot extending to the right. On the right is a blue shape with slanted edges, with a peak at the upper left, a dip in the top edge in the middle, and a sloping right side. Neither shape has labels or printed values.
figures.original: Do you think that these shapes have the same area? Check and find out.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A square grid with three shapes drawn on it: a right-angled triangle at top left, a tilted square (diamond) at top right, and a rectangle at bottom left. The triangle has a vertical side of 5 squares and a horizontal base of 4 squares. The diamond has its corners at the midpoints of its sides and spans 4 squares across and 4 squares high. The rectangle is 4 squares wide and 2 squares high. A ladybird, a caterpillar and an ant are drawn as small decorations near the shapes.
figures.original: What is the area of each shape? How do you know?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A triangular (isometric) grid of grey lines with two shapes outlined in orange and shaded blue. On the left is a large equilateral triangle with one vertical side on the right and its point on the left, each side 3 small triangle edges long. On the right is a regular hexagon with each side 3 small triangle edges long. A green cartoon frog sits at the bottom left and a brown frog at the bottom right. No numbers or words are printed.
figures.original: What is the perimeter of each shape? How do you know?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: An orange square with a dark outline. The top side is labelled 2 cm and the right side is labelled 2 cm.
figures.original: What are the perimeters of these shapes?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A dark purple rectangle on a light blue background. The top side is labelled 8 m and the right side is labelled 7 m.
figures.original: What are the perimeters of these shapes?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A blue parallelogram with a diagonal line from the top left vertex to the bottom right vertex. The diagonal divides it into two equal triangles. There are no labels or numbers.
figures.original: If this is 2/4 of a shape, draw what the whole shape could look like.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Four outlined shapes in a row, each with a fraction label beneath it. From left to right: a six-pointed star labelled 1/4, a four-pointed star labelled 1/4, a pentagon-like shape with a pointed right end labelled 1/2, and a double-headed arrow shape labelled 1/2. The shapes are not divided.
figures.original: Draw lines to divide these shapes into equal parts according to their labels.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A rectangle (a tile) is split by diagonal lines into regions, some shaded blue and some white. A diagonal runs from the top left corner to the bottom right corner. A second diagonal runs from the top left corner to the bottom edge, at about the middle of the left half. A third diagonal runs from the top edge, at about the middle, to the bottom right corner. The shaded blue regions are the left triangle beside the left edge and the parallelogram-shaped band in the upper middle. The white regions are the thin triangle in the middle and the triangle at the upper right. No labels or numbers are printed.
figures.original: This tile shows a pattern made with fractions. What fraction of the tile is shaded?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A large square with dashed lines drawn inside it: a vertical line and a horizontal line through the centre, plus both diagonals from corner to corner. These lines meet at the centre and divide the square into 8 equal triangles. The lines are dashed and the square has a solid border. Nothing is shaded or labelled.
figures.original: Use this square to create a design with a different fraction shaded. Some of the dotted lines may help.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A rectangle is divided into a top row of two equal cells, each labelled 1/2. The bottom row is divided into four equal empty cells. To the right is the equation 1/2 = (empty box) over 4, with the numerator box left blank.
figures.original: Use these fraction strips to find equivalent fractions. Write the correct fraction in the boxes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A fraction strip with a top row of five equal boxes, each labelled 1/5. Below it is a second row divided into ten equal, unlabelled boxes, with two of these boxes under each 1/5 box. To the right is the equation 1/5 = □/10, with the numerator box left empty.
figures.original: Use these fraction strips to find equivalent fractions. Write the correct fraction in the boxes.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3

figures.original: What fraction of the whole strip is shaded? Draw a ring around your answer.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3

Three are analogue clocks with numbers 1 to 12: d has a purple frame, the minute hand points near 10 and the hour hand points near 5. e has a black and white patterned frame, the minute hand points at about 3 and the hour hand points near 4 to 5. f has a blue frame, the minute hand points at 9 and the hour hand points near 4 to 5.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3

figures.original: Count the number of sides in each shape. For each shape, divide it into the same number of equal parts as the number of sides. Colour two parts in each shape. What fractions are coloured?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3

figures.original: Count the number of sides in each shape. For each shape, divide it into the same number of equal parts as the number of sides. Colour two parts in each shape. What fractions are coloured?

figures.original: Write the time that is shown on each digital clock.

figures.original: Write the time that is shown on each digital clock.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A 3 by 3 grid of squares with a single digit in each square. Row 1 reads 1, 3, 2. Row 2 reads 2, 5, 3. Row 3 reads 3, 4, 1.
figures.original: Choose three different 3-digit numbers to add by reading across or reading down the grid. Estimate and then solve your addition. Show your method.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Two place value grids, each with columns labelled 100s, 10s and 1s. The top grid has 2 blue counters in the 100s column, 4 red counters in the 10s column and 6 green counters in the 1s column. An arrow points down to an empty grid with the same three column headings.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A measuring jug with a pouring spout on the upper left and a scale in ml on the right side, labelled from 100 to 1000 in steps of 100 with smaller unlabelled tick marks between them. The jug contains blue liquid whose surface is at about the 400 ml mark.
figures.original: To the nearest labelled division, write how much liquid is in these containers.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A measuring container (beaker) with a millilitre scale on the right side, labelled from 100 to 600 with 'ml' at the top. Long tick marks are labelled 100, 200, 300, 400, 500 and 600, and shorter unlabelled ticks lie between them. The container is filled with blue liquid up to a level just above the 100 mark, at about 150 ml. The letter 'b' is printed at the top left.
figures.original: To the nearest labelled division, write how much liquid is in these containers.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: An analogue clock with a green rim and a white face. It shows the numbers 1 to 12 around the edge, with minute tick marks. The short hour hand points at 8. The long minute hand points close to 1, which is 5 minutes past the hour.
figures.original: Write the times below each clock.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: An analogue clock with a pink rim and a white face. The numbers 1 to 12 are printed around the face, with minute tick marks around the edge. The short, thick hour hand points to just before 11. The longer minute hand points at about the 3, slightly below it. Both hands meet at a pink centre dot.
figures.original: Write the times below each clock.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: An analogue clock face with an orange rim and the numbers 1 to 12 printed around it, with minute tick marks. The short, thick hour hand points just past the 2, and the long, thin minute hand points to the 7. Both hands are dark grey and meet at an orange centre dot.
figures.original: Write the times below each clock.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: An analogue clock with a purple rim and the numbers 1 to 12 printed around the face, with minute tick marks. The short hour hand points between 1 and 2. The long minute hand points at about the 7, close to the 6 and 7 side of the face. The crop shows a small red mark in the top left corner.
figures.original: Write the times below each clock.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A round analogue clock face with a purple rim and a purple dot at the centre, but no hands. The numbers 1 to 12 are printed around the face, with minute tick marks around the edge. Below the clock the time 9:12 is printed.
figures.original: Draw the hands on these clocks to show the times. d 9:12

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Three monthly calendars side by side: January (orange header), February (green header) and March (blue header). Each has columns headed M, T, W, T, F, S, S. January starts on Friday 1 and ends on Sunday 31 (Saturday 2, Sunday 3 in the first row). February starts on Monday 1 and ends on Sunday 28. March starts on Monday 1 and ends on Wednesday 31.
figures.original: Use the calendar to find the answers.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A train timetable with a header row: Destination, Train 1, Train 2, Train 3, Train 4, Train 5, Train 6. The rows are Brightville, Blue City, Central Town and Downton, each with a departure time for each train. Some cells hold a dash, and the Central Town cell for Train 3 is blank.
figures.original: Here is part of a train timetable.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A timetable with six columns, each headed by a subject, with a time printed beneath it. Maths is 9 – 10 a.m., Science is 10 – 10.45 a.m., Art is 11 – 11.30 a.m., Music is 12 – 12.30 p.m., Games is 1 – 2.15 p.m. and Literacy is 2.30 – 3.15 p.m. The lower part of each column is empty.
figures.original: a What time does the art lesson start?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A bird's-eye map of a town with compass arrows labelled north (top), south (bottom), west (left) and east (right). Grey roads run between green blocks of houses. The school is in the upper middle, next to a roundabout. The park, with a swing, a slide and trees, is in the upper right, reached by a diagonal road from the roundabout. Also shown are a post office, a bank, a library, a police badge, a red barn, plates with cutlery, shopping baskets and trees.
figures.original: How could you get from the school to the park? Tell your partner how to get there.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A table titled "Train timetable" with columns for First train, Second train, Third train and Fourth train, and rows for Blueberry Hill, Sunny Meadow and Redwood Place. Blueberry Hill: 7:30, 8:05, 8:25, 9:20. Sunny Meadow: 7:47, – (no stop), 8:42, 9:39. Redwood Place: 8:00, 8:40, 8:59, 10:00.
figures.original: Grandma wants to go to Sunny Meadow from Blueberry Hill. What time does the earliest train leave the station?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A circle with a single straight arrow inside it. The arrow starts at the centre and points straight up to the top of the circle, where its head touches the circle. There are no other marks, labels or numbers.
figures.original: a a quarter turn clockwise

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A large circle with a single arrow drawn from the centre straight up to the top of the circle, with the arrowhead touching the circle at the top. There are no labels or numbers.
figures.original: b a quarter turn anticlockwise

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A timetable with columns for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, and rows for the times 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 1:00 and 2:00. Monday: Walk, Swimming, Lunch, Football, Tennis. Tuesday: Reading, Swimming, Lunch, Walk, Games. Wednesday: Reading, Swimming, Walk, Lunch, Tennis. Thursday: Walk, Reading, Lunch, Singing, Tennis. Friday: Walk, Swimming, Lunch, Bike ride, Tennis.
figures.original: This timetable shows activities for a week at holiday camp.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A central picture of three tents (red, blue and orange) on grass represents the campsite. Four orange arrows point away from it, labelled north, east, south and west. North leads to a stone bridge over a river, east to a group of trees (forest), south to a pond with rocks and grass, and west to a school building with a clock.
figures.original: You are at the campsite. a What can you see if you look west?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A grid of 6 columns and 8 rows of squares with a thick dark route drawn on it. The route starts at the top edge, at the right end of the top row (the label 'start' is above it), and goes down one square, then west four squares along the first grid line. It then goes south four squares, east one square, and south four more squares to the bottom edge, where the label 'finish' is printed. A compass rose beside the grid shows N at the top, E at the right, S at the bottom and W at the left.
figures.original: Imagine that you are facing south. Write the instructions for the route from start to finish. Use the words left, right and forward.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Eight flat colored shapes on a pale blue background. Top row: a pink triangle with all sides about equal, a purple rectangle, and an orange right-angled triangle. Middle row: a red-orange pentagon, a blue L-shaped polygon with six sides, and a yellow speech-bubble shape with a small pointed tail. Bottom row: a purple five-pointed star and a green circle.
figures.original: Count the right angles inside these shapes. Mark them.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A table with two column headings, 'Possible' and 'Impossible', and four rows of statements. The statements are 'A horse will grow wings and fly.', 'A carrot will walk.', 'A baby will cry.' and 'It will rain somewhere in the world today.' All the answer boxes are empty.
labels: A horse will grow wings and fly.
It will rain somewhere in the world today.
figures.original: Are these things possible or impossible? Put a tick in the box.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A grid of 3 rows and 7 columns, where some squares hold labelled pictures of places. Top row: School in column 2 and Play area in column 6. Middle row: Library in column 3 and Police station in column 7. Bottom row: Bus stop in column 1, START HERE in column 4 and Supermarket in column 6. All other squares are empty.
figures.original: Write the instructions to get from START HERE to the school.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A rectangular array of dots in 5 rows of 11 dots each, evenly spaced. The top-left dot is labelled 'start' with an arrow pointing to it, and the bottom-right dot is labelled 'finish' with an arrow pointing to it.
figures.original: Join the dots to get to the finish. Each dot is a step.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A table with four columns headed 'Letter on spinner', 'Will/Will not/Might happen', 'Estimate how many times' and 'Actual number of times, as a tally'. The letters A to F are listed down the first column, one per row. The only other entry is 'might happen' in the row for A, and all remaining cells are empty.
labels: Actual number of times, as a tally
figures.original: Try it and see. Use tally marks to keep a record of the results.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Six dominoes in a row, each split into a top half and a bottom half by a line. From left to right the halves show: 1 spot above and 1 spot below; 2 spots above and 2 spots below; 0 spots above and 4 spots below; 1 spot above and 4 spots below; 1 spot above and 6 spots below; 4 spots above and 6 spots below.
figures.original: You have these six dominoes in a bag. What is the chance that if you take out one domino, the total number of spots is more than eight? Draw a ring around the answer.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A table with three column headings: "Will happen", "Might happen" and "Will not happen". There is one row. The letter "A" is written in the "Might happen" cell. The other two cells are empty.
figures.original: Write the event's letter in the correct section in the table.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A circular spinner divided into three equal sections by lines from the centre. The top left section is orange and labelled 1, the top right section is green and labelled 2, and the bottom section is blue and labelled 3. The letter A is printed below the spinner.
figures.original: a What might happen if you spin spinner A? Write down all answers.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A circular spinner divided into 8 equal sectors, each a different colour and numbered 1 to 8 clockwise from the top right: 1 orange, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 red/salmon, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 olive green, 8 pink. The spinner is labelled with the letter B below it.
figures.original: b What might happen if you spin spinner B? Write down all answers.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A green outline of a composite shape made of two joined rectangles. The left rectangle is taller and the right one is shorter and sits to its right, so the top edge steps down from left to right. A dashed horizontal line runs along the bottom, and the shape's base lies on it. The right edge of the shape stops at the dashed line, and the dashed line extends a little past both sides. A partly visible red letter sits at the far left edge of the crop.
figures.original: Sketch the reflection.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A small letter "b" appears in the top left corner. An orange outline of a downward-pointing chevron (V-shaped arrow) is drawn on the left of a vertical dashed grey line, which acts as the mirror line. Nothing is drawn on the right side of the line, so the reflection is left for the learner to sketch.
figures.original: Sketch the reflection.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A pink outline of a rhombus (a diamond shape) standing on one of its vertices, with its lowest point touching a horizontal dashed line below it. The dashed line is the mirror line. There are no labels or numbers.
figures.original: Sketch the reflection.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A vertical dashed line is the mirror line on the right. A blue shape touches it: a straight line runs from a point on the mirror line down and to the left to a vertex. From that vertex a curved arc sweeps down and to the right, back to the mirror line at a lower point. Together these form a wedge or sector shape with the dashed line as its right side. A red letter "d" is at the top left.
figures.original: Sketch the reflection.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A red polyline sits above a horizontal dashed black line that acts as a mirror line. The red line starts on the dashed line at the left, rises steeply to a high peak, drops to a lower valley, rises to a second, lower peak, then drops almost vertically back to the dashed line near the right end. A partial letter 'a' appears in red at the top left edge.
figures.original: Sketch the reflection.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: An orange zigzag line shape lies to the left of a vertical dashed mirror line. The shape starts at the top of the dashed line and goes down-left, then zigzags with horizontal steps and slanted segments. It ends with a long slanted line to the bottom left and a horizontal line back to the dashed line at the bottom. The letter b is printed at the top left.
figures.original: Sketch the reflection.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A Venn diagram inside a rectangle labelled "Numbers". Two overlapping circles: the left circle is labelled "Even" and the right circle is labelled "Multiples of 3". The overlap region and the two outer parts of the circles are empty, and no numbers are written in any section.
figures.original: If Zara and Arun can think of numbers to put in each of the three sections of the Venn diagram, they get to keep the cards and they get two points.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A round orange-yellow smiley face with an orange outline. It has two round eyes, each a white ring with a dark center, and a curved smiling mouth filled with white. The face is symmetrical left to right, and no line of symmetry is drawn.
figures.original: Draw a line of symmetry on each shape.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A single light blue crescent (moon) shape with a thin dark outline. The two curved edges meet at pointed tips at the top right and bottom right, and the bulge of the crescent faces left. No line of symmetry is drawn and there are no labels.
figures.original: Draw a line of symmetry on each shape.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A shape made of green squares on a white background, with a vertical dashed line on the right side that acts as a possible line of symmetry. One green square is at the top left, and another is at the bottom left. A wider green band runs across the middle, with a notch cut out of its lower edge. The band extends to the right past the dashed line. The dashed line passes through the right part of the shape.
figures.original: 4 Which of the diagrams shows symmetry?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A green pattern made of squares on a white background, with a horizontal dashed line across it. Above the line are two separate squares at the top left and top right, and a wide rectangle below them that spans the middle and crosses the dashed line. Below the line is a single square in the centre, then two squares below it to the left and right, then two squares at the bottom left and bottom right. The upper and lower parts of the pattern are not mirror images of each other across the dashed line.
figures.original: 4 Which of the diagrams shows symmetry?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A green shape like a capital letter I, with a wide horizontal bar at the top, a narrower vertical stem in the middle, and a wide horizontal bar at the bottom. A dashed horizontal line runs across the figure, through the stem a little below the middle. A letter 'c' in orange is partly visible at the top left.
figures.original: 4 Which of the diagrams shows symmetry?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a woven textile pattern in dark grey and light pink strips. The strips form a repeating grid of diamond shapes. Each diamond is made of nested stepped outlines with a small dot at its centre. The diamonds are arranged in staggered rows across the whole image.
figures.original: Can you see any lines of symmetry in this pattern?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Eight coloured shapes in two rows of four, each with an empty tick box beneath it. The top row has a blue rectangle, a dark purple isosceles triangle, an orange right-angled triangle and a green parallelogram. The bottom row has an orange circle, a blue cross shape, a blue regular pentagon and a pink arrow-like chevron shape with a notch cut into its left side.
figures.original: Tick the shapes that have at least one line of symmetry.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Three identical blue-purple circles are stacked vertically in one column, each touching the one above or below it. There are no labels or numbers.
figures.original: Starting with these three circles, three circles are added each time to extend the pattern. Complete the number sentences.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Two identical blue-purple squares are drawn side by side and touch each other, forming one wide rectangle with a vertical line down the middle. There are no labels, numbers or other markings.
figures.original: Starting with these two squares, two squares are added each time to extend the pattern. Complete the number sentences.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A symmetrical pattern made of six shapes: a red regular hexagon in the centre, a yellow hexagon on its left and another on its right, and blue rhombuses (diamonds) at the top left, top right, bottom left and bottom right. A vertical dashed line runs down the middle through the red hexagon. The pattern is the same on both sides of the line, and the top half matches the bottom half.
figures.original: This pattern shows both vertical and horizontal symmetry.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A green line pattern made of a hexagon-like shape with a rectangle in the middle and a triangle-like pair of diagonal lines on each side, sitting above a small green square. A vertical dashed line runs through the centre of the pattern as the line of symmetry. The top part is a wide horizontal band with slanted sides, divided by a horizontal line across its middle. The small rectangle hangs below the bottom edge, centred on the dashed line.
figures.original: This pattern has one vertical line of symmetry to show the reflection. Add some shapes to the pattern so it also has a horizontal line of symmetry. Draw the horizontal line of symmetry.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Half of a shape is drawn in green on a light teal background, standing on a horizontal dashed line. The left part is a tall rectangle, and to its right is a shorter rectangular step whose right edge drops down to the dashed line, so the outline looks like an L or staircase. The other half of the shape is not drawn.
figures.original: Complete the shapes on the other side of the line of symmetry.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Two dashed lines cross at right angles. One is vertical and one is horizontal, and they meet near the centre of the picture. Nothing else is drawn and there are no labels or numbers.
figures.original: Use these lines as lines of symmetry.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: Two identical orange circles are stacked vertically and touch each other. Below them is the number 2.
figures.original: Starting with these two circles, extend the pattern by adding two more circles. Do this three times.

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A horizontal line with a tick mark at each end. The left end is labelled "Will not happen" and the right end is labelled "Will happen". A downward arrow above the middle of the line points to the midpoint.
figures.original: What event could Marcus say? Why?

figures.textbookName: CAMBRIDGE PRIMARY MATHEMATICS LEARNERS BOOK3
figures.shows: A horizontal line with a tick at each end. The left end is labelled "Will not happen" and the right end is labelled "Will happen". A downward arrow points at the left end tick, which marks the position Sofia chose.
figures.original: What else could Sofia have chosen to say? Why?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A horizontal number line with arrowheads at both ends and 11 evenly spaced tick marks between them. The tick marks at the second position from the left and the one at the far right are not labelled, and the taller tick in the middle is labelled 6000. The tick labelled 5500 is the third from the left. A bold downward arrow above the line points at the second tick from the right end.
figures.original: What is the number shown by an arrow on each number line? (b)

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A horizontal number line with arrowheads at both ends and evenly spaced tick marks. The longer tick marks are labelled 7000 and 8000, with shorter unlabelled ticks between them and one just beyond each labelled tick. A blue arrow above the line points down at a tick between 7000 and 8000, which is past the midpoint.
figures.original: What is the number shown by an arrow on each number line? (c)

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A horizontal number line with arrowheads at both ends and evenly spaced tick marks. The ticks at the left and right are labelled 5500 and 6000. There are 10 intervals between 5500 and 6000, and a tall bold arrow points down to the tick just before 6000, the second-to-last tick on the line.
figures.original: What is the number shown by an arrow on each number line? (d)

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A table with four rows and nine columns listing place-value numbers. The top row is 1000 to 9000, the second row is 100 to 900, the third row is 10 to 90, and the bottom row is 1 to 9. Four numbers are printed in red: 3000, 500, 70 and 1.
figures.original: Write each red number in figures, words and expanded form. (a)

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A table with 4 rows and 9 columns of place-value numbers. Row 1 reads 1000 to 9000 in thousands, row 2 reads 100 to 900 in hundreds, row 3 reads 10 to 90 in tens, and row 4 reads 1 to 9. Three numbers are printed in red bold: 1000 (first row, first column), 900 (second row, last column) and 9 (fourth row, last column).
figures.original: Write each red number in figures, words and expanded form. (b)

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Three digit cards are shown side by side, slightly tilted. The left card is yellow and shows 1, the middle card is pink and shows 8, and the right card is green and shows 7.
figures.original: Pablo has these digit cards. He makes three-digit numbers with the cards. Write down all the numbers he could make.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Three number cards are arranged in an overlapping cluster. A pink card reads '39 hundreds', an orange card reads '390 tens', and a green card reads '39 tens'.
figures.original: Look at these number cards.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Four rows, each with a number on the left, a green arrow pointing right, and an empty answer box marked with a question mark on the right. Above each arrow is a phrase. The rows read: 3000 'is one hundred less than' ?; 5000 'is one hundred more than' ?; 6500 'is one thousand more than' ?; 980 'is one hundred less than' ?.
figures.original: Find the missing numbers.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Five traffic-style cones in different colours, each printed with a number: red 12, orange 7, blue 8, green 13 and yellow 5. Four purple hoops lie on the ground near the yellow cone. Four yellow stars show target totals: 22, 31, 50 and 27.
figures.original: Throw hoops over the cones to make the totals in the stars. All four hoops must land on a cone. There can be more than one hoop on a cone.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Three ovals joined by blue arrows. The top-left oval contains 6. An arrow labelled ×10 goes from it to a right-hand oval containing a question mark. An arrow labelled ×10 goes from that oval to a bottom oval containing a question mark. A separate arrow labelled ×100 goes from the 6 directly to the bottom oval.
figures.original: (a) Copy the diagrams below. Write down the missing numbers.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A diagram with three oval boxes connected by blue arrows. The top oval contains 1400. An arrow labelled ÷10 leads from it to a middle oval containing a question mark. An arrow labelled ÷10 leads from the middle oval to a bottom oval containing a question mark. A second arrow labelled ÷100 leads directly from 1400 to the bottom oval.
figures.original: (b) Copy the diagrams below. Write down the missing numbers.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Three oval boxes are joined by blue arrows. The top-left oval holds 32. An arrow labelled ×10 goes from it to a middle-right oval that holds a question mark. From that oval an arrow labelled ×10 goes to a bottom-left oval that holds a question mark. A second arrow labelled ×100 goes directly from the 32 oval to the bottom oval.
figures.original: (c) Copy the diagrams below. Write down the missing numbers.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Three oval boxes joined by arrows. The top oval holds 8000. An arrow labelled ÷10 leads from it to a middle oval containing a question mark. An arrow labelled ÷10 leads from the middle oval to a bottom oval containing a question mark. A separate arrow labelled ÷100 leads directly from the 8000 oval to the bottom oval.
figures.original: (d) Copy the diagrams below. Write down the missing numbers.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A grid of 5 rows and 4 columns of numbers, with Start in the bottom-left cell and Finish in the top-right cell. Row 1: 4, 8, 2, Finish. Row 2: 9, 1, 4, 6. Row 3: 8, 5, 5, 2. Row 4: 2, 4, 3, 8. Row 5: Start, 1, 7, 9. A blue example route line runs from Start up the first column to 8, right to 5, up to 1, left to 9, up to 4, then right along the top row to Finish.
figures.original: Make a route through the grid from Start to Finish. You can move horizontally or vertically. Add up the numbers on your route. Find the route that gives the lowest total.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A spider diagram with a central red circle containing 2. Eight lines run out from it, each passing through an empty square marked with a question mark and ending in an outer red circle. The outer circles read 12 (top left), 14 (top), 6 (top right), 18 (left), 16 (right), 20 (bottom left), 8 (bottom) and 4 (bottom right).
figures.original: Look at the spider diagrams for the 2× table. Copy the diagrams and fill in the missing boxes.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A spider diagram with a central circle containing 2. Nine circles connect to it, labelled 2×2, 7×2, 9×2, 10×2, 4×2, 3×2, 8×2 and 6×2. Each outer circle is joined to an empty square containing a question mark, where the answer goes.
figures.original: Look at the spider diagrams for the 2× table. Copy the diagrams and fill in the missing boxes.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A 4 by 4 grid of sixteen three-digit and two-digit numbers. Two cells are shaded light yellow: 228 in the top right and 672 in the third row, first column. The shaded pair is the example that adds to 900.
figures.original: Find five pairs of numbers that add up to 900. One has been done for you.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A cartoon map of a neighbourhood of houses and roads. Fred's house is at the top left and a shop is at the bottom right. Red arrows show one-way paths between yellow stars, and each star has a number, which is the cost of that step. The stars are numbered 37, 11, 24, 27, 29, 18, 15, 23, 34, 20 and 9. Arrows run from Fred's house to 37, 29 and 34. Other arrows link the stars to each other, and several lead to the shop, such as from 27, 23 and 9.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Fifteen colourful toy cars are drawn in 3 rows of 5, with no labels or numbers. Most are ordinary cars in red, blue, green, grey, orange and yellow. Some are different shapes: a red van-like car, and purple or yellow-green wedge-shaped racing cars with a small driver.
figures.original: Which expressions can he use to find the total number of toy cars?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4

figures.original: What is the missing number?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4

figures.original: Copy these tables. Use doubling to complete these table patterns.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: Three triangles made of colored sticks, labelled pattern 1, pattern 2 and pattern 3. figures.original: How many sticks would be needed to make pattern 7?

figures.shows: A table with two columns headed "Pattern number" and "Number of sticks". The rows show pattern 1 with 3 sticks, pattern 2 with 6 sticks, and pattern 3 with 9 sticks.
figures.original: How many sticks would be needed to make pattern 7?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4

Pattern 1 is a small square with 4 sticks: one on top, one on the bottom, one on each side. Pattern 2 is a rectangle with 2 sticks on the top, 2 on the bottom and 2 on each side, 8 sticks in all. Pattern 3 is a larger rectangle with 3 sticks on the top, 3 on the bottom and 2 on each side, 10 sticks in all. Each stick is a different color.
figures.original: How many sticks would be needed to make pattern 9?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
figures.shows: A table with two columns headed "Pattern number" and "Number of sticks". It has three rows: pattern 1 has 4 sticks, pattern 2 has 8 sticks, and pattern 3 has 12 sticks.
figures.original: How many sticks would be needed to make pattern 9?

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4

figures.original: Use a number line to show how to calculate 23 × 4 using repeated addition.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Stage 4 Learners Book 4
